mechanism: Work on the scalar face H = C − 2E at the exact samples X_m = m(m+2). Abel-sum the Mertens weights in the kernel-checked reciprocal family so E(x) becomes Σ_d μ(d)·[prime-count − Li] on (x/(d+1), x/d], with pure μ(d) coefficients; because X_m/m = m+2 and X_m/(m+2) = m are exact integers, the hyperbola reflection d ↔ q at the corner d = m is an exact involution with no fractional boundary defect (kernel-checkable identity). Now use the window of H consecutive square samples r = 0..H−1 as the dispersion family: expand the window energy Σ_r |E(X_{N+r})|², open the square, and note X_{N+r} = X_N + r(2N+2) + r², so each off-diagonal pair (d,e) of reciprocal indices, after sawtooth/Fourier expansion of the interval endpoints with frequencies h, h', carries the quadratic phase γ(r² + 2(N+1)r) in r with rational frequency γ = (he−h'd)/(de) of denominator dividing [d,e]·(h-range). Weyl differencing on the r-variable gives square-root gain H/q^{1/2} whenever the effective denominator q ≤ H^{2−ε}, and the map (d,e,h,h') ↦ q has divisor-bounded multiplicity ≪ q^ε — an explicit shared-modulus construction with sub-square multiplicity. The prime-discrepancy (non-sawtooth) component of the variance consists of prime counts in intervals moving by ≈ rX/d² as r runs, i.e. short-interval PNT at heights x/d with lengths ≥ H·N/d·(scale); for H ≥ N^{7/12+ε} every d-block clears the Huxley 7/12 threshold, giving error exp(−c(log N)^{1/3}) [adjacent-lens input: zero-density, itself built on van der Corput sums]. Net effect: window energy = H·|window mean Ē_{N,H}|² + variance, and the variance is bounded unconditionally with the stated savings; all RH-hard content collapses into the single scalar Ē_{N,H} per window. The payoff of the collapse: the pinned critical block d ∈ (N^{1−δ}, N] of E is, at fixed x, a one-variable μ(d)·1_prime(≈x/d) correlation (Chowla/Sarnak-hard, parity-blocked); inside the window mean it becomes a genuine two-variable bilinear form in (d, r) with r-length ≥ N^{7/12}, restoring the Type-II structure that parity-evading Vinogradov methods require. The angle therefore does not claim to close rung 2; it claims to reduce the Gram/window target, unconditionally and with explicit losses, to a single smoothed pinned scalar on which bilinear machinery has structural purchase where the raw pointwise object provably has none.
new_leverage: Three things a standard application would not give. (1) The averaging family is manufactured from the construction itself: the square-sample index r inside the window supplies ~H arithmetically explicit shifts X_{N+r} − X_N = r(2N+2) + r², turning the pinned reciprocal family into incomplete quadratic Weyl sums — this directly answers the declared claim that "no family of shifts/moduli to average over" exists. (2) The exact corner X_m = m(m+2) makes the hyperbola reflection an involution with integer corner values, so the bilinear decomposition of E has no secondary main term and the sawtooth expansion has no boundary wobble — a property generic x never has and which the packet's square sampling was presumably designed for but which standard treatments discard. (3) An explicit off-diagonal-to-shared-modulus map (d,e,h,h') ↦ q | [d,e]·h-range with q^ε multiplicity, refining obstacle 2 from "no map known" to a sharply located failure set q > H^{2−ε}; and the window-mean collapse converts the parity-hard one-variable critical block into a bilinear (d,r) form.
target_estimate: Square-Gap Variance theorem (SGV), the estimate I would actually prove: for every ε > 0 there are c(ε) > 0 and N_0(ε) such that uniformly for N ≥ N_0 and N^{7/12+ε} ≤ H ≤ N, with X_m = m(m+2) and Ē_{N,H} = H^{-1}Σ_{r<H} E(X_{N+r}), one has Σ_{r<H} |E(X_{N+r}) − Ē_{N,H}|² ≪_ε H·N²·exp(−c(log N)^{1/3}) , where the sawtooth/rounding component of the variance separately satisfies the stronger power-saving bound ≪ H·N^{2−c'} for moduli q ≤ H^{2−ε} (Weyl gain H/q^{1/2}, multiplicity q^ε), and the prime-discrepancy component carries the exp(−c(log N)^{1/3}) loss inherited from zero-density short-interval PNT at the 7/12 threshold. Corollary (the transfer): for windows with H ≥ N^{7/12+ε}, the exact Lean target ProjectedRenewalQuadraticBoundedStatement restricted to those windows follows from the single-scalar bound |Ē_{N,H}| ≪_ε N^{1+ε} together with the corresponding statement for C (same machinery, easier since C is all-plus and zero-mode-centered). Losses: N^ε from divisor sums throughout; exp(−c(log N)^{1/3}) from the zero-density input; the constraint H ≥ N^{7/12+ε} from the Huxley threshold; no claim for H < N^{7/12}.

obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Partially answered, partially conceded. Answered: the window supplies an internal shift family r < H with explicit quadratic phases, so no external averaging over starts is invoked and W_{k-1} is never placed in an exceptional set — the dispersion runs inside one synchronized block. Conceded: the H = 1 instance of the Lean statement is the pointwise scalar face, so pinnedness is irreducible; my mechanism relocates the pinned content into the single window mean Ē_{N,H} rather than eliminating it. Risk specific to synchronization: the Weyl frequencies 2(N+1)(he−h'd)/de could be abnormally well-approximable when N sits near primorial synchronization (many small d dividing structured quantities), inflating the no-gain set; this is testable (see kill test).
obstacle_positions.large_sieve_non_transfer: Directly engaged. I exhibit the missing construction: off-diagonal pairs (d,e) with sawtooth frequencies (h,h') map to the shared modulus q dividing [d,e]·(frequency range), with multiplicity ≪ q^ε (divisor bound) — sub-square. What survives of the obstacle is exact and located: the Weyl gain requires q ≤ H^{2−ε}; with H ≤ N and q up to N², the block [d,e] > H^{2−ε} (essentially d,e ~ N coprime) receives no gain and is exactly critical at the target scale — the obstacle is refined to a named critical set, not removed.
obstacle_positions.not_bombieri_vinogradov: Agreed and respected. No residue-class averaging over moduli is used anywhere; the averaging variable is the window index r, and the reciprocal intervals remain disjoint ordinary intervals. The short-interval prime input is Huxley-type (ordinary intervals), not BV-type. No claim of well-factorable weights or moduli families.
obstacle_positions.strong_induction_failure: Respected by construction. Mertens weights M(d) are Abel-summed to μ(d) before any bound is taken, and the dispersion acts on the squared window energy directly; at no point is |M(d)| ≤ Kd^{1/2+ε} inserted into the family, so the divergent operator Σ Λ(m)m^{-1/2}-type loss identified by the route document never appears. The signed C − 2E combination is kept intact inside the window mean; only the variance is bounded by absolute-value methods, which is safe because the variance is the part I prove small unconditionally.
obstacle_positions.parity: Stated honestly: not broken, relocated. The bilinear (Type II) structure from Vaughan decomposition evades parity in the sub-critical blocks, but on the pinned critical block d ~ N the object degenerates to the one-variable correlation μ(d)·1_prime(≈x/d), where bilinear independence vanishes and parity (indeed Sarnak-conjecture hardness) applies with full force. The window-mean collapse restores two-variable (d,r) bilinearity there, which is the structural precondition for parity evasion — but I make no claim that the resulting bilinear form is currently estimable at rung-2 strength at a pinned N. Parity is this angle's terminal wall, and it sits exactly in the scalar Ē_{N,H}.
obstacle_positions.finite_range_deception: The deliverables are proved, not measured: the corner involution is a finite kernel-checkable identity, SGV is an unconditional theorem, and the rung-0 closure is classical machinery. Numerics enter only through the kill test, which is a mass-location diagnostic (where does the variance live), not an exponent fit; a near-flat empirical exponent would neither support nor be cited for any claim here.

kill_test: Cheapest kill: a mass-location computation, not an exponent fit. For a few blocks with N ≈ 3·10^4 (so x ≈ 10^9, one segmented sieve) and H = ⌈N^{2/3}⌉, compute E(X_{N+r}) for r < H via the reciprocal family, center at the window mean, and decompose the variance by dyadic ranges of d. If ≥ 90% of the window-centered variance sits in d > N^{1−o(1)} — the one-variable μ×prime critical block where q = [d,e] > H² and no Weyl gain exists — then the dispersion machinery addresses a vanishing fraction of the object, SGV becomes true-but-empty, and the angle is dead as leverage. Secondary cheap check of the synchronization risk: restrict to prime pairs d,e ∈ (N/2, N] (so q = de exactly) and evaluate the r-sum Σ_{r<H} e(X_{N+r}(1/d − 1/e)) for many pairs; if the observed cancellation is systematically absent for windows placed near primorial boundaries (versus mid-block placement), the pinned-frequency degeneracy risk is real and the uniform-gain bookkeeping fails.
rung0_plan: At o(x)/PNT strength the same machinery closes end to end with no critical-block gap. Apply the exact-corner reflection, then Vaughan's decomposition to both the μ(d) weight and the prime indicator in the reflected bilinear form. Type I sums Σ_{d~D} a_d Σ e(h x/d)-shape (smooth long variable) are handled by van der Corput exponent pairs — the phase hx/d has monotone derivative and the h = 0 mode is absent by the wheel's exact zero-mode elimination (contraction ρ < 1/6), which is precisely the term that dominates in the classical unwheeled setting. Type II bilinear blocks are handled by Cauchy–Schwarz plus Vinogradov's shift argument. The window mean Ē and the prime-discrepancy variance are both controlled by the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region, giving E(X_n), C(X_n) ≪ X_n·exp(−c(log X_n)^{3/5−ε}) and hence window energy ≪ H·N⁴·exp(−c'(log N)^{3/5−ε}) — the rung-0 form of the Lean statement (exponent 4 in place of 2+ε, with the exp-log saving certifying non-triviality). Every step is classical and effective; writing it in the exact wheel/square coordinates is bounded work and doubles as a correctness audit of the reindexing.
plausible_partial: Realistically provable at bounded effort: (1) the exact-corner involution identity for the reciprocal family at X_m = m(m+2), as a finite combinatorial statement suitable for kernel-checking — settles that the bilinear reflection has zero boundary defect; (2) the SGV theorem as stated, for H ≥ N^{7/12+ε}, with power saving on the sawtooth component and exp(−c(log N)^{1/3}) on the prime component — inputs are Weyl differencing, divisor bounds, and Huxley-grade short-interval PNT, all off-the-shelf; (3) the transfer corollary reducing the window form of the Lean target (in the range H ≥ N^{7/12+ε}) to the single-scalar bound |Ē_{N,H}| ≪ N^{1+ε}; (4) the rung-0 closure above. Explicitly not plausible from this lens: any rung ≥ 1 bound on Ē itself or on the pointwise face — the Korobov–Vinogradov ceiling caps the lens below every fixed θ < 1, and the H = 1 instance shows the target is pointwise-RH-hard; the value of the package is the unconditional collapse of the H-dimensional Gram window onto one smoothed scalar per window with restored bilinear structure.
self_assessed_risk: The assumption most likely to be false: that a non-vanishing share of the window-centered variance of E lives at moduli q = [d,e] ≤ H^{2−ε} where the Weyl and Huxley gains operate. If the variance concentrates in the top block d ~ N — plausible, since the shortest reciprocal intervals carry the least averaging and the μ×prime one-variable correlation there is exactly the parity/Sarnak-hard core — then SGV is provable but empty: the reduction moves nothing, the "restored bilinearity" of the window mean is the whole problem restated, and this lens has no further purchase. Secondary risk: uniformity of the Weyl gains at pinned synchronized N (frequency degeneracy near primorial boundaries), which would poison the bookkeeping in exactly the blocks the construction pins.
